title: Turla hackers use new Cereal malware to spy on govt Exchange servers
content_md: The Russian state-backed threat group Turla has been using a new malicious toolset called 'Cereal' to intercept emails on Microsoft Exchange servers at government organizations. Researchers at cybersecurity company ESET documented the attacks in late 2025, initially finding modular .NET malware for Microsoft Exchange at a government body in Kazakhstan. A month later, ESET found the same toolset at a government agency in Romania, where it selectively gathered email correspondence with representatives of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) and the European Union (EU). "After fine-tuning our detections, we found the same toolset at a governmental organization in Romania - compromised on December 23rd, 2025," the researchers say in a report today. Turla, also known as Snake, Secret Blizzard, and Waterbug, is a cyber-espionage group active for more than two decades and linked to Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB). In the campaign analyzed by ESET, the hackers use the Cereal toolset, and specifically a component in the kit named CerealBox, to inject into Exchange’s EdgeTransport.exe process and hijack existing transport agents’ handlers. The malware executes commands in memory and can inspect email content without registering a new transport agent or interrupting normal email delivery in the Exchange server.
